sources.basis: Original Go interpretation of container/volume superblocks, object maps, filesystem B-tree records, inodes, streams, attributes and Fletcher 64. Native qualification is separate. Keylocker, ONEKEY and extent crypto_id interpretation follow the encryption chapter; native evidence qualifies outer XTS keybags and current extent flag 1 where published details are incomplete. Snapshot metadata/name records, physical snapshot superblocks and transaction-bounded historical resolution are original interpretations of the snapshot and object-map chapters. Fresh construction uses the container/checkpoint, object map, space manager, B-tree, inode/stream, hard-link sibling and extent-reference structures. Native fsck and continued macOS allocation independently qualify the constructed state. Multiple-volume construction uses nx_fs_oid slots, per-volume fs_index, reserves/quotas, group UUIDs and SYSTEM_OBJ_ID_MARK. The latter is independently observed in native System user objects and apfs_next_obj_id; UNIFIED_ID_SPACE_MARK is not used as the allocator base. Existing APFS mutation is an original Go implementation of the published object storage classes, B-tree/object-map versioning, space-manager CIB/bitmap/internal-pool structures, transaction-tagged free queues and checkpoint mappings. Native macOS 15/26/27 source/peak/final captures separately qualify observable file semantics and allocator state; Apple fsck, mounted readback and continued native/Go/native mutation are required. Stored resource-fork stream IDs differ from owning inode IDs; physical extent owning_obj_id follows the owning filesystem record. The actual checkpoint descriptor is selected when block zero has the same XID with different native counters. Directory mutation uses published directory-entry hashes, inode child/link counts, volume file counters, primary sibling selection, sibling-link/map records and apfs_next_obj_id. Native retained create/move/unlink/removal states independently confirm retained single-sibling records and primary-name/parent repair; fresh Apple checker/readback and native/Go/native cycles qualify the writer. Adjacent free-queue range coalescing retains the published transaction lifetime. No private APFS kernel C implementation is claimed as a source port. Existing-image metadata patches and generic attribute stream mutation are original interpretations, independently qualified by macOS 15/26/27 metadata controls. Native ordinary streams carrying the unpublished 0x10 flag use their stream ID for physical extent ownership, unlike legacy attributes/resource forks. The writer preserves this observed distinction, rejects unknown flags/shared profiles, and requires native continued writes; no private flag name or C port is inferred. Link creation inserts sibling-link/map records for original and new aliases while retaining original inode/stream identities, and stores literal symlink targets in filesystem-owned attributes. Native first-link, alias growth/replacement/removal and signed framework controls qualify these original Go interpretations. Native copy controls expose adjacent data/resource-fork ranges coalesced under one physical owning_obj_id. Admission accounts nonoverlapping physical ranges by current stream ownership, and retirement splits the physical record while retaining surviving prefixes/suffixes. Shared streams and clones remain refused. Resource forks remain stream-backed regardless of size in both construction and mutation. macOS 15/26/27 fsck in run 38265407088 independently rejected an 18-byte embedded copied fork; mutation admission now refuses that shape, and boundary/clear regressions require the resulting image to remain editable. Checkpoint completeness follows pp. 26–27 and 40–42: transaction-bound mapping sequences and ephemeral objects, selected ring ranges, checksums, identities and object type/subtype validation. One original Go decoder serves reads, explicit inspection/recovery and mutation. Unsupported checkpoints never authorize rollback; selected object-map/tree/ownership damage is refused. Recovery disables rejected newer descriptors and refreshes block zero after complete ownership admission. A damaged checksum can only supply bounded locator hints corroborated by an independently checksummed descriptor with identical immutable geometry. Native run 38298298833 supplies genuine checkpoint-data/mapping/superblock/ring-wrap windows and separately declared one-byte damage controls on macOS 15/26/27. Apple checker XIDs and mounted metadata/fork/signature observations are independent expectations. Earlier-state controls explicitly disable the damaged descriptor before Apple checking; no Apple repair of original damaged input is claimed. Every-write prefix/ENOSPC/failed-acknowledgement controls and portable/native continued allocation qualify file-backed recovery, not in-place flush ordering or physical power loss. Completed software conversion admission follows APFS_INCOMPAT_ENC_ROLLED (historical key changes) separately from apfs_er_state_oid (a nonzero in-progress transition). The reader exposes the rolling-state OID, refuses unfinished conversion before filesystem/keybag access, and admits the historical flag only for reads. Native completed encryption, changed-password, shared encrypted edits and decryption states independently qualify this distinction; writer admission is unchanged. Storage ownership uses the signed int32 physical extent counts, unsigned stream counts, chronological NEW/UPDATE trees retained by snapshots, transaction-bounded object-map predecessors and explicit checkpoint/free-queue lifetimes. Reserved omap snapshot oms_oid bytes are not physical roots. General ownership permits a valid original physical owning_obj_id to outlive its original inode; ordinary writer admission still requires exclusive owners. Idle empty reaper list pages are decoded separately from active work. Native sparse inode allocated bytes include INO_EXT_TYPE_SPARSE_BYTES; subtracting and validating hole coverage reconciles physical extents without inferring addresses from allocation totals. Older checkpoint descriptors are disabled in the unpublished copy before deferred-block reuse; the selected checkpoint survives publication failures. Fresh checkpoint capacity follows the documented four-generation minimum and separately budgets the emitted free-queue node limits, complete space manager, reaper, first reaper-list page and advertised per-volume ephemeral structures. The doubled per-volume allowance is conservative engineering policy corroborated by retained Apple-created geometries, not a published Apple sizing formula or a bound on arbitrary future native workloads. Descriptor capacity includes multiple checkpoint maps and one container superblock per generation; raw geometry remains within existing reader limits. The public fragmented-delete and continued-allocation regression independently proves a Go mutation capacity defect without attributing native pressure failures.

sources.licenseBasis: Apple table and HFS source headers specify APSL 2.0. The Unicode scalar normalizer additionally acknowledges Unicode and IBM/ICU; those copyright notices and their permission texts are retained in generated source and LICENSES.

sources.basis: Independent native lstat lookups include Unicode 11/14/16 case pairs, hard-link aliases share st_ino/st_nlink and all forks/metadata, and F_LOG2PHYS_EXT proves more than eight physical extents per fragmented HFS+ data/resource fork. Decoder-only translation adapted from the inventoried v2 production port. Reviewed against Corellium libzbitmap C; this is not Apple-published source. Output is caller-owned and bounded before each chunk. Apple public-codec output and native filesystem reads provide independent qualification.

Only production decoder algorithms were retained, with upstream notices; no tests, encoders, decmpfs Handle or legacy filesystem orchestration imported. LZ4 framing is a v2 original MIT implementation, not an Apple C port; v3 requires complete bounded frames. Each codec is independently requalified from fresh native observations.

Original bounded reader and zlib writer using the documented decmpfs_disk_header layout, maximum attribute size and UF_COMPRESSED admission behavior. Fresh type-3/type-4 storage uses Go standard-library zlib and independently observed Resource Manager framing; no Apple encoder implementation is copied. Native public-codec decoding, kernel reads, continued writes, fsck and signatures independently qualify output. Codec storage framing was studied from v2 production and independently installed/read on native volumes. XNU dispatch and kernel cnode implementation are not copied. Replacement also studies decmpfs_decompress_file, unset_compressed_flag and decmpfs_free_compressed_data: zero truncation clears UF_COMPRESSED and frees codec-owned storage plus the decmpfs attribute. No kernel code translated; original Go storage transitions are independently checked by native O_TRUNC writes. Unlike native writes, the preservation API keeps recorded source timestamps and marks modified contents explicitly. Compression admission also follows decmpfs_hides_rsrc/decmpfs_hides_xattr: all active compressed files hide their resource fork, independent of compression type. Fresh zlib construction therefore refuses compression for files with independent forks, including small type-3 candidates, preserving ordinary native fork visibility as well as raw bytes. macOS 15/26/27 readbacks in run 38111101888 independently exposed the earlier incorrect type-3 exception.

Native ditto supplies LZVN filesystem storage. Apple public compression codecs supply other encoded payloads; final read-only kernel reads and public-codec decoding of stored bytes are independently compared. Types 1,3,4,7-16, stored markers, zlib optional checksum and resource descriptor gaps are exercised. Only 0xff is admitted as an LZFSE stored marker: a native malformed zero-marker file reports logical size but returns premature EOF; Go rejects it rather than synthesizing contents. macOS 15/26 may reject LZ4 types 15/16 at the filesystem layer even when their public codec decodes the stored bytes; CI records both outcomes explicitly.

GPL source studied for format facts: UUID-derived XTS outer bags, HMAC cookie, KEK/VEK DER layout and extent tweaks. No code copied or translated. Original bounded Go parsing and standard cryptographic constructions are independently checked against native Apple-created images. Legacy flag-2 key records remain explicitly unsupported.

Keybag entry alignment and key-record field study. DER lengths are big-endian. Structural and HMAC validation precede bounded password derivation; undocumented profiles do not fall through to authentication failure.

Header/API study only; no CommonCrypto C implementation copied or linked into Go. Native CCCryptor XTS, CCKeyDerivationPBKDF and CCSymmetricKeyWrap/Unwrap supply independent public vectors. AES-256-XTS vectors do not qualify a native APFS volume cipher profile.
Original bounded RFC 3394 unwrap with mandatory constant-time IV integrity verification, built on Go standard AES.

Original bounded multi-block PBKDF2 implementation with cancellation. APFS uses HMAC-SHA256 and encrypted DMG password records use HMAC-SHA1. Native CommonCrypto vectors and Apple-created images independently qualify the derived keys.

Production-only lessons; no test/harness material imported. v3 separates failed credentials, damaged key records and unsupported profiles, bounds aggregate derivation, validates HMAC and RFC3394 integrity, and uses per-extent tweaks. No v2 orchestration or cryptographic code copied.

Four Apple-created software-encrypted APFS volumes, 108 objects each, ordinary/Unicode/long/changed passwords and native rejection controls. Fresh read-only mounts with ownership enabled provide file and metadata hashes, including compressed files and modified clones. Native key records use flags 0, 40-byte wrapped keys, keybag version 2 and extent flag 1. Primitive reference bytes are independently generated with CommonCrypto. Broader key profiles require additional native evidence.
Published CSSM constants identify AES, 3DES, SHA1HMAC, PKCS5_PBKDF2, CBC_IV8, CBCPadIV8 and PKCS7 in native encrypted-image headers. Format identifiers studied; no Apple implementation copied.

Version 2 header, key-table and password-record layouts, PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA1, key-cookie and per-block IV derivation studied. Original bounded Go interpretation; no Python code copied or translated. Native macOS evidence independently qualifies AES wrapping and both payload key sizes.
Older encrypted-image layout and 3DES password-wrapping facts cross-checked against vfdecrypt. No C implementation copied or translated; fixed-offset and AES-128-only assumptions are not inherited.

Six Apple-created AES-128/256 encrcdsa v2 images cover APFS, case-sensitive APFS, HFS+, HFSX, UDZO and raw UDRW, Unicode/changed/rejected passwords and an independently encrypted APFS volume. Each has 107 observed objects from a final read-only mount. Current native password records wrap with AES-192-CBC, declare an 8-byte IV and use a zero-extended 16-byte AES IV. Retained capture and file/source hashes are immutable; older wrapping profiles require their own native CI evidence. Writer layout follows the observed 616-byte password slot, 122368-byte reserved header, 512-byte encrypted blocks and AES-192 password wrapping. It generates fresh cryptographic randomness and uses a fixed 600000-iteration derivation within the captured native range. Native output acceptance is required separately; the reader round trip is not its compatibility verdict.

Public snapshot enumeration and attribute ABI studied for an original Python ctypes collector. Kernel entitlement checks explain direct-call rejection; no kernel implementation copied. Apple asr and mount_apfs perform native snapshot creation and retention on disposable volumes. The supported name-based create/rename/revert APIs are observed by an original C helper signed with the public developer snapshot entitlement. Actual syscall status/errno and signed-tool identity distinguish successful mutation from an explicit EPERM linked to the positive-control blocker. The fsctl_internal dispatcher explicitly rejects APFSIOC_REVERT_TO_SNAPSHOT before APFS; its kernel-only revert fallback does not establish a supported userspace XID interface. No private ioctl layout or private entitlement is inferred.

Apple-created replication snapshots, UUID/XID inventory, native timestamps and final read-only historical mounts independently qualify two historical states alongside live state in ordinary, case-sensitive and nested encrypted APFS. The first saved superblock has no extended metadata OID; the live OID resolves the snapshot UUID at its XID. Unicode snapshot names and non-leaf snapshot metadata trees remain unqualified.

Four native APFS/HFS+/HFSX images, 125–126 entries each. Final read-only observations include logical file hashes, raw XATTR_SHOWCOMPRESSION values, native metadata, link identities and host-incompatible names. Apple copyfile independently packs/unpacks three metadata controls per filesystem. Portable output returns to macOS for an independent Python preservation comparison and native unpack, without invoking Go.

Four native before/after APFS/HFS+/HFSX images, 14 entries and seven content replacements each. Inactive malformed attributes survive. Portable results preserve before timestamps by policy while content/fork/link outcomes match after observations. Four native before/after APFS/HFS+/HFSX profiles with 18 operations, eight rejection controls and six name-length probes each. Four native before/after APFS/HFS+/HFSX profiles, 29 operations and seven rejections each. Go translation of setmode/getmode numeric and symbolic mode instructions. Explicit logical umask replaces process umask reads and signal masking; slices replace C allocation and instruction compaction. Native libc independently supplies 390 expression/mode/mask vectors per filesystem profile.

Command and traversal policy study; no cp implementation translated. Apple -a means -RpP and splits hard links; --preserve-links is an explicit portable extension. Independent native commands qualify the packaging journey; process authorization, account-name lookup and kernel caches are outside the logical session contract. Four native before/after filesystem profiles, 23 Apple commands and five rejection controls each. noatime mounts avoid lazy read-cache effects. Copied provenance remains exact; native process-injected provenance on new objects remains recorded but is outside portable process-authorization behavior. Local ownership uses same-owner assignment; required CI must change owners with sudo.

Immutable macOS 15 CI reference with actual UID/GID reassignment to 60001/60002. Native capture passed on all three Macs; the first portable replay exposed that physical recursive chown changes symlink ownership while chmod skips symlinks. The corrected implementation passes these saved native observations. This reference prevents same-owner local capture from hiding the difference.

Study of reserveBlocks, f_bfree/f_bavail and hfs_freeblks explains physical versus caller-available block accounting, including loaned/locked blocks and sparse-device backing-store limits. No kernel allocation implementation is copied. The formatter's InitVH accounting remains separately inventoried. All three disposable native VMs build the same macOS 15 APFS/HFS+/case-sensitive sources using Apple automatic sizing and explicit Go capacity. Apple cannot populate the old 9,052,160-byte APFS capacity; its 18,337,792-byte automatic image admits at least 8 MiB of new native data. Measurements establish underprovisioning without claiming an exact private Apple formula or universal reserve constant. Fresh output qualification retains complete native modification/fsck/remount workloads.

Adapted InitVH, WriteExtentsFile, WriteAttributesFile and WriteCatalogFile header/map initialization to a fresh-volume Go planner. Core format/link/xattr sources guide catalog, current regular-file hard-link chains and extent-based attributes. No kernel mutation or journal implementation is ported. Contiguous payload allocation, bounded bulk-loaded trees, explicit UTC clock and content-derived identity replace device writes, native defaults and random UUIDs. Native fsck and mounted observations independently qualify output. Allocation bitmap initialization follows makehfs zeroing and MarkExtentUsed: only real allocated extents and the header blocks are marked; padding beyond totalBlocks stays clear. The independently studied CheckVolumeBitMap compares the entire final 1024-bit segment, exposing the old incorrect all-ones padding when automatic capacities end within a segment. Fresh hard links follow hfs_makelink/createindirectlink and cat_createlink: kHFSHasLinkChainMask is set on inode and aliases; inode reserved1 stores hl_firstLinkID, and alias BSD owner/group fields store hl_prevLinkID/hl_nextLinkID. Actual UID/GID remain on the inode. Legacy flagless construction was readable, but cat_lookup marks resolved inodes as chained and subsequent native writes persist an incomplete chain. CheckHardLinks exposed that transition during compression replacement in run 38114955455. Stored-record regressions inspect complete three-alias chains in plain/compressed HFS+/HFSX output; native continued modification remains the independent verdict. Matched retained native controls independently expose the fresh lastMountedVersion and allocationFile.clumpSize fields: InitVH uses kHFSPlusMountVersion (10.0), and hfsplus_params rounds the required bitmap bytes to allocation blocks. The Go nonjournaled builder now uses that identifier and bitmap clump size.

Apple-created HFS+/HFSX inputs include a signed universal app, hard links, exact native metadata, attributes, independent resource forks and decmpfs types 1/3/4/7/8. Portable outputs are checked by hdiutil verify, fsck_hfs -fn, read-only native file observations and codesign on each Mac. A native encoder diagnostic established the 4 MiB maximum uncompressed UDIF chunk and checksum-covered type-0 zero runs; formatter probes established the attributes fork clump field and HFSX private-folder count flag. Source observations are retained unchanged.

Production-only study of UDIF checksum/blkx/footer fields, cross-checked against native hdiutil conversion. Original sequential Go encoder; no v2 tests, orchestration or code copied. Fixed 4 MiB chunks, bounded XML and explicit exact-source-length failures. Repacking also studies production-only block reconstruction, device/partition variants and signature footer offsets. Original strict resource admission and complete-coverage/CRC verification replace permissive reconstruction; no v2 tests were read or imported.

Original format research cross-check for flattened UDIF footer flags, device/partition variants, block resources and native plst placeholder. Reference only; no prose or implementation copied. Apple-tool acceptance supplies the independent compatibility verdict.

Apple-created raw, UDRO, UDZO and UDBZ disks; native raw-device full-disk SHA-256 and mounted file, fork, attribute, partition/volume, snapshot and encryption observations. Reuses independent signed-app and snapshot inputs with recorded parent provenance. Apple partitionDisk creates an APM free partition before seeding an unused sector; expected marker bytes are then read through the native device. Native signed and encrypted DMGs are explicit refusal controls. Every portable host output returns to each required Mac; no Go code supplies the native verdict. Native readback rejected a generic single-block device descriptor for raw APM input; native conversion supplies DDM/APM and GPT region descriptors, and raw-device hashes prove the resulting disk remains identical.

Production-only format study: space-manager geometry and native free-queue limits, checkpoint mapping, APFS B-tree records, name hashing and hard-link/document records. Original bounded container planner borrows filesystem.Reader and streams sorted output rather than importing v2 Entry trees, host adapters or mutation APIs. No v2 tests or harness imported. Apple format facts and independent native checks determine acceptance. Volume-group root/private IDs and reserve accounting were studied, but the v2 System user-inode base was rejected after a native kernel panic. Apple SYSTEM_OBJ_ID_MARK and captured native allocator state replace that assumption.

Expanded independent macOS 27 reference includes APFS and case-sensitive APFS alongside HFS+/HFSX, signed universal applications, exact birth/modification/change/access times, tracked documents, 53 filename lookup observations, links, attributes, forks, compression and an empty-directory construction root. Native fsck, mounted comparisons, codesign and writes through disposable shadows followed by check/remount qualify Go output. Prior HFS-only capture is retained unchanged under history. Local evidence does not replace the required macOS 15/26/27 CI matrix.

Independent Apple-created shared and grouped containers provide UUIDs, per-volume reserves/quotas/case/roles, group inventories, signed application trees and inode namespaces. Native shadow writes establish bounded quota/reserve enforcement, protected-volume allocation, independent writes and reuse after remount. Original references and copied capture sources remain immutable. Full macOS 15/26/27 capture, portable replay and VM-isolated native readback qualify output; fsck alone is insufficient.

BitMapCheckBegin captures real volume headers and initializes all other bits clear. CheckVolumeBitMap compares complete 1024-bit segments with memcmp, including final padding, and reports extra set bits as orphaned allocation. No checker code is copied. macOS 15/26/27 run 38113498604 rejected the old bitmap in a 2631-block volume, whose final segment incorrectly marked 441 nonexistent blocks. Portable regressions fail on the old output and independently check clear tail bits and consistent free counts; fresh native fsck remains required.

CaptureHardLink, inode_check and CheckHardLinks distinguish legacy flagless links from current kHFSHasLinkChainMask records and validate chain heads, reciprocal pointers and counts. No checker code is copied. Native compression writes exposed the mismatch between legacy constructed aliases and inodes whose chain flag the kernel persists during an update.

ExtendBTreeFile requests synchronous primary/alternate header flushing after system-file growth. The separately inventoried hfs_vfsops writer copies updated metadata to the alternate header. Checker debug output identifies catalog total-block disagreement and invalidates the alternate header. No kernel/checker code copied; native route controls and exact raw-sector copying qualify the original Go filesystem independently. The alternate-header addressing macros are studied against captured logical/physical geometry. Storage-only writes isolate shadow replay without mounting HFS; the public source is not used to invent private DiskImages internals.

The Go HFS+ filesystem, its Apple UDRO rewrap, and an Apple UDRW conversion receive the identical mutation/check/remount workload. Apple-rewrapped shadow writes leave stale 92-block alternate headers after the primary catalog grows to 100 on all three Macs; converted direct writes pass with matching headers. One original shadow control passes on macOS 15, recording variability. Stronger admission in run 38120590877 rejects UDRW conversion because sector hashes change despite equal device capacity; those successful converted controls cannot independently qualify the original disk. Acceptance instead streams exact Apple-attached sectors to private raw copies and requires native full device size/hash equality plus original image preservation before writes. No repair or failed-checker exception is admitted. Private DiskImages internals are not inferred from this evidence.

Complete captures at macOS 15.7.9/24G830, 26.6.2/25G83 and 27.0.1/26A434 retain all 48 matched Apple/Go HFS+/HFSX growth controls and 21 unmounted native sector probes. Direct raw writes and 16 MiB shadows pass; 10,936,320-byte Apple and Go shadows expose a stale ten-block alternate catalog after primary growth to 34. Blank Apple UDRO probes reproduce acknowledged tail writes present in the detached shadow but absent from read-only reopened device sectors. The size ends 8192 bytes into a 16384-byte native VM page; independently chosen 16 KiB-aligned controls pass without 32/64 KiB alignment. Writable reopen outcomes remain separate and can alter the actual shadow bytes. This isolates the observed failure below HFS and Go construction, but does not claim private DiskImages internal code or a universal OS-specific rule. Compressed original manifests, complete disks, source envelopes, actual shadows, tool/recipe provenance and native failed checker verdicts are committed; file-only replay checks exact hashes, metadata/forks and unchanged native expectations after archive deduplication.

Go adaptations of VolumeAllocation bitmap marking/accounting, hfs_extents grouping/coalescing, BTreeTreeOps SearchTree/SplitLeft/DeleteTree/CollapseTree, BTreeNodeOps record offsets, and BTreeAllocate AllocateNode/FreeNode. Exclusive unpublished regular-file copies replace mounted vnodes, tree path tables, locks and journal callbacks. Deterministic first-fit allocation and byte-balanced splits omit kernel allocation caches and optional sibling redistribution. Original Go admission verifies complete allocation ownership, native keys, node maps/reachability, and both structural headers. Catalog changes patch original fixed-size records, retaining CNIDs and opaque bytes. Nonjournaled volume-header signature follows hfs_flushvolumeheader. Active compression removal shares existing decmpfs ownership policy. Explicit offline timestamps and no-overwrite completed-image publication are project policy, not kernel credential emulation, HFS journal recovery or universal power-loss durability. Native evidence is supplied by the existing-hfs-file-edits family on disposable macOS 15/26/27 VMs; its producer never invokes Go. The native preservation control supplies birth/access times explicitly with mtime: hfs_vnop_setattr otherwise clamps HFS+ creation time to an older new modification time. Guard allocation records actual ENOSPC instead of assuming statfs availability is synchronously current. Metadata/attribute mutation adapts hfs_vnop_setattr, hfs_set_bsd_flags, hfs_vnop_setxattr/removexattr, hfs_buildattrkey and getmaxinlineattrsize. Attribute-key names use unnormalized binary UTF-16 ordering; FinderInfo keeps reserved catalog fields and private symlink values. Offline clock assignment and credential admission remain explicit project policies. PR32 native readback independently exposed missing kHFSFileLockedMask synchronization: BSDInfo alone reported user immutable offline while Apple getbsdattr cleared it. Shared catalogBSDFlags/setCatalogBSDFlags adapt getbsdattr/catrec_update reconciliation and Finder hidden mirroring. File lock is authoritative, legacy locked files supply UF_IMMUTABLE, and directories retain their separate record rules. Explicit chflags clears user locks while protected system immutable remains refused. Resource-fork setxattr delegates to VNOP_WRITE at the supplied offset without truncation. Position-zero short writes retain existing tails and allocated HFS fork storage; zero-byte writes have no data effect. The same rule is independently observed on APFS. Separate full-fork replacement remains the cp/named-fork operation. Portable prefix composition reads current-transaction APFS records, retaining old data until retirement permits reclamation, and remains bounded for large tails. Complete copy resource-fork replacement is separate from hfs_vnop_setxattr prefix writes. Native hfs_vnop_listxattr gates compressed resource visibility through decmpfs_hides_rsrc unless XATTR_SHOWCOMPRESSION is supplied; explicit active-compression native controls qualify this distinction.

Adapted calc_checksum, journal_is_clean and current journal_open header/geometry checks to bounded byte slices. Checksums cover the original 44 bytes before sequence_num, with the checksum field zeroed in stored byte order. hfs_late_journal_init supplies backing-file location/size checks; disagreement is refused rather than relocating, recreating or disabling a journal. hfs_flushvolumeheader supplies HFSJ versus 10.0 mount identifiers. hfs_is_journal_file supplies CNID-based protection for both journal backing files. Admission requires a clean volume and current, empty, initialized internal journal with contiguous catalog-backed allocation; size is bounded from 256 KiB to 1 GiB. Exclusive unpublished copies preserve complete journal/JIB storage and sequence numbers, with no live journal transactions.
